title: 2012 Knox Legal Studies Trial
notes: The PDF contains no answer key. Questions 15–18 share the scenario printed on page 6; no non-text figures are needed. all answers are reasoned guesses.

groups.stimulus: After years of physical abuse and repeated death threats, Catherine enlists the help of her son Silas to kill her husband, Darren. She shoots Darren while he is watching television. Silas helps plan the murder and buries Darren’s body afterwards.

questions.stem: What is the role of the Director of Public Prosecutions?

options.A: To make recommendations regarding criminal law reform
options.C: To protect the public from crime
options.D: To prosecute offenders in the District and Supreme Court

questions.answerNote: The DPP prosecutes serious criminal matters on behalf of the state.

questions.stem:
The Government of Gillardia passes a statute allowing mining companies to release unprocessed waste water into rivers. Protesters can be arrested and imprisoned without trial if they attempt to prevent water releases.

Which of the following rights are being violated?

options.A: Economic, social and cultural rights and the collective right to self determination
options.B: Civil and political rights and the individual right to self determination
options.C: The right to a clean environment and economic, social and cultural rights
options.D: Civil and political rights and the right to a clean environment

questions.answerNote: Imprisonment without trial infringes civil and political rights, while pollution threatens the right to a clean environment.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a public order offence?
questions.answerNote: Offensive language in public is a public order offence.

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of bail?

options.C: To protect the rights of the accused

questions.answerNote: Bail preserves the accused person’s liberty and presumption of innocence while proceedings continue.

questions.stem:
Kai has been in foster care since he was eight. He left school at 13 and has committed a series of increasingly serious offences ever since. He is now on trial for armed robbery.

Which of the following factors affect Kai’s criminal behaviour?
questions.answerNote: Foster care and leaving school early are social factors; A (environmental) is a weaker alternative.

questions.stem:
Alex is charged with sexual assault after his DNA is found on the victim’s clothes. His defence lawyer introduces witnesses who testify that Alex was at work at the time of the crime.

Which element of the crime is Alex disputing?
questions.answerNote: The alibi disputes that Alex committed the prohibited act.

questions.stem: Which purpose of punishment is achieved by fining a speeding driver?
questions.answerNote: A speeding fine is usually taught as deterring drivers generally; A (specific deterrence) is also plausible.

questions.stem: Which of the following people is most likely to receive legal aid?

options.A: An accused with no prior offences who is pleading not guilty
options.B: A young offender who is pleading not guilty
options.C: An accused with prior offences who is pleading guilty
options.D: An accused person with a mental illness

questions.answerNote: Young offenders are a priority group for legal aid; D (mental illness) is also plausible.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a characteristic of summary offences?

options.A: They are heard by a jury in a local court.
options.C: They are only punishable by a fine.

questions.answerNote: Summary offences are the less serious category and are generally dealt with summarily.

questions.stem:
Patrick stabs Julia in the course of a robbery. He then calls an ambulance. At the hospital, Julia refuses a blood transfusion because she believes that the doctors are trying to poison her. She dies and Patrick is charged with her murder.

Which element of the crime can Patrick dispute?
questions.answerNote: The refusal of treatment may be raised to dispute the causal link between Patrick’s act and Julia’s death.

questions.stem:
The Federal Parliament passes a statute protecting freedom of speech.

How is this right now enforceable?

options.A: By the High Court using the Charter of Rights
options.B: By customary law recognised in tribunals

questions.answerNote: A statutory right can be enforced through the courts and tribunals applying the legislation.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of social crime prevention?

options.A: A program to get truants back to school
options.B: Security guards and closed-circuit cameras in a shopping centre
options.C: Drug detection dogs at a concert

questions.answerNote: School engagement addresses social conditions associated with offending.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an intergovernmental organisation which promotes human rights?
questions.answerNote: The European Union is an intergovernmental organisation with human rights responsibilities.

questions.stem:
The High Court of Australia overturns a statute limiting welfare payments to indigenous people on the grounds that the government is violating international law.

Which of the following best describes how human rights have been protected?
questions.answerNote: The question states the High Court acted because of a breach of international law; A fits the stem as written, though in reality Australian courts cannot strike down statutes on that basis.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes Silas’ role in the crime?

options.A: He is an accessory before the fact.
options.B: He is the principal in the first degree.
options.C: He is the principal in the second degree.
options.D: He is an accessory after the fact.

questions.answerNote: Silas helped plan the murder (accessory before the fact); D is plausible because he also buried the body, but the planning is his role in the crime.

questions.stem: What is the main reason for providing Catherine with legal aid?

options.A: To achieve fairness in the adversary system
options.B: To improve Catherine’s compliance with the legal system
options.C: To help her as she is disadvantaged

questions.answerNote: Legal aid exists mainly so an accused facing the state's prosecution has proper representation, which makes the adversary system fair; C is plausible but the scenario never says Catherine is disadvantaged.

questions.stem: If you were Catherine’s lawyer, which defence would you advise in order to obtain an acquittal?
questions.answerNote: The repeated abuse and death threats support an argument that Catherine acted to protect herself from threatened harm.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is true?

options.B: The Prosecution must prove Catherine’s defence.
options.D: The judge must prove to the jury that Catherine’s defence has no precedent.

questions.answerNote: The accused must raise sufficient evidence to put a defence in issue; The prosecution then bears the applicable burden to disprove it.

questions.stem: Which of the following rights is promoted in the Universal Declaration of Human Rights?

options.B: The right to freedom of religion
options.D: The right to trial by jury

questions.answerNote: The UDHR protects freedom of thought, conscience and religion.

questions.stem: When do police in NSW have the right to take a blood sample?

options.B: When they have a court order
options.C: When a young offender gives consent
options.D: When there is reasonable suspicion the suspect committed the crime

questions.answerNote: A court order is an authorised route to obtain a forensic sample where consent is not otherwise available.
